chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Monopolizing (al-hukrah) is when one buys food that is not available in the city except from him, so he hoards it. So if there is food in the city, or if others are selling it, there is no problem with seeking a premium price for his goods.
He (the narrator) said: And I asked him about oil, so he said: If it is with others besides you, there is no problem with withholding it.

key_terms.الْحُكْرَةُ: Monopoly or hoarding of goods to control price

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between monopoly (hukrah) and permissible price negotiation in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the conditions for 'hukrah' (monopoly) by distinguishing between absolute scarcity, where hoarding is prohibited, and relative scarcity, where withholding goods to seek a premium is permissible. It highlights the Shia juristic focus on market dynamics, noting that the prohibition applies specifically when a commodity is unique to the seller within the city, whereas common goods like oil allow for strategic withholding. This reflects the practical application of price control mechanisms in early Islamic markets to prevent exploitation during shortages.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The monopoly is in that when food is bought, and there is nothing in the city apart from it, so it is monopolised. So if there was (sufficient) food in the city, or someone else was selling it (as well), so there is no problem with seeking the preferential price’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the oil, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was with someone other than you, so there is no problem with withholding it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Hoarding means buying such food supplies of a city beside which no other food supplies are available. If other food supplies are available in a city or someone else sells food, then it is permissible to buy food supplies and keep them hoarded to sell later with higher prices.’
He (the narrator) has said, I asked him about oil and he replied, ‘If it is available with people other than you then there is no offense in it.’”
